Nevada Alert
Jan 1, 2027:
Watering Your
Grass Becomes Illegal
Nevada's restriction on decorative turf irrigation takes effect in 6 months. Here's what to do.
Shop Drought-Tolerant Seed

On January 1, 2027, Southern Nevada's restriction on decorative turf irrigation takes effect. Ornamental grass in medians, commercial strips, and HOA common areas can no longer be watered with Colorado River water. Residential decorative turf that isn't functional is also targeted for phase-out.
The realistic path forward is to convert decorative turf to drought-tolerant native species that don't need supplemental irrigation once established. Bermudagrass blends, buffalo grass, and the Southwestern Wildflower Mix are the regional standards — proven on Las Vegas, Henderson, and Boulder City conversions for years.
To get ahead of the deadline, drought-tolerant seed needs to be in the ground by October 2026 at the latest to allow establishment before winter. That's about four months from now to order, plant, and water in. After that, you're waiting until spring 2027 — past the deadline.
